turns.content: One of my friends has made jokes about me being stupid in front of other people several times.

I'm sorry to hear that. It can be really hurtful when friends make jokes at our expense, especially in front of others. Have you had a chance to talk to your friend about how their comments make you feel? Sometimes, people don’t realize the impact of their words.
Last week I told them privately that those jokes embarrass me and asked them to stop.

It’s great that you spoke up about how you feel. Setting boundaries is important in any friendship. Have they responded to your request? If they continue to make those jokes, it might be worth considering how that affects your friendship and whether you need to have another conversation about it.
They did it again yesterday and laughed when I reminded them I'd asked them not to.

I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds frustrating and hurtful, especially after you expressed your feelings. It might be time to have a more serious conversation with them about how their behavior is affecting you. You deserve to be treated with respect, and if they continue to dismiss your feelings, it could be worth reevaluating the friendship. How do you feel about addressing it again?
They're probably just being playful and don't mean anything by it, right?

It’s possible they think they’re being playful, but that doesn’t make it okay, especially since you’ve already expressed that it bothers you. Playfulness shouldn’t come at the expense of someone’s feelings. It’s important for friends to respect each other’s boundaries. If you feel comfortable, you could try explaining that while you understand they might not mean any harm, their jokes still hurt you. How do you think they might respond to that?
